title: Half-life: how a radioactive sample decays
goal: See how much of a radioactive sample is left after each half-life.
note: Every half-life, half of the radioactive nuclei that are left decay. The sample here starts at 480 decays per second and has a half-life of 6 minutes, so the time control moves in whole half-lives.

graphs.title: The activity halves every half-life, so the curve falls steeply and then flattens.
graphs.label: Activity left

sentences: After one half-life half of the sample is left, after two half-lives a quarter, after three an eighth, and so on.
Each step of the time control is one half-life.

predict.prompt: The activity starts at 480 per second. What will it be after two half-lives?
choices: A quarter of the starting activity
predict.reveal: Move the time control to 12 minutes, which is two half-lives, and read the activity.

concept_check.question: A sample has a half-life of 6 minutes. How much of it is left after 12 minutes?
concept_check.explanation: 12 minutes is two half-lives. Half is left after the first and half of that, a quarter, after the second.

hints: Half of the sample decays in each half-life.
How much is left after one half-life? And after two?
Keep halving the amount once for every half-life that has passed.
